question.text: A molecule undergoes two independent first order reactions whose respective half lives are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>min</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>min</mi></math>. If both the reactions are occurring then the time taken for the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></math> consumption of the reactant is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>min</mi></math>. (Nearest integer)

solution.text:
For parallel reaction

When adding the rate constants of the two reactions, we need to use the formula for combining rate constants of two reactions in parallel, which is:

k=k1+k2

where k1 and k2 are the rate constants of the individual reactions.

In this case, the half-lives of the two reactions are 12 min and 3 min, respectively. The rate constants of the two reactions can be calculated using the formula for half-life of a first-order reaction:

1t1/2=112+13=512

Net t1/2=125=2.4 min≈2 min

Hence time taken for 50% consumption of reactant will be close to 2 min.
